a package manager that installs project dependencies

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Scripts and version requirements
sections.what: Defines the named commands for build, dev servers, lint, test, typecheck, database and Docker, plus the required Node and pnpm versions.
sections.why: Gives each task one name that every developer and the CI can use.
sections.watch_out: The docker build script depends on a production compose file that is not in the packet.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Developer tools and commit checks
sections.what: Lists developer tools and the rules that format and lint staged files and check commit messages.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps code and commit history consistent.
sections.watch_out: Commit message format is enforced only when the git hooks are installed.

summary: The root project file. It names the monorepo, lists the common commands, the developer tools, and the commit-check rules.
purpose: Gives one place to build, test, lint, format, start dev servers, and run database tasks across all apps.
why: Standard for a Node.js monorepo. The commands hand their work to Turborepo, which runs them across packages.
how: pnpm reads the scripts section, and each script names one task. Developer tools are installed from the dev dependencies. Husky sets up git hooks, and lint-staged runs lint and format on staged files.
inputs: Read by pnpm, Turborepo, and the git hooks.
outputs: Runs the named commands and enforces commit message format.
risks: The docker build script refers to docker-compose.prod.yml, which is not in the packet. The clean script deletes node_modules. The database reset script is destructive.
debug: If a script fails, run it alone and check the package named in its filter. Confirm Node 20 or later and pnpm 9 or later are installed.
